stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function in language tasks.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, relevant to the AI community.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates continued community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's Llama models.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption on Apple Silicon hardware.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating active development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It leverages local AI coding agents, enabling AI functionality to run entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI capabilities for coding assistance.

stories.title: Sony pushes forward with ditching discs, despite backlash
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Sony is proceeding with the discontinuation of physical game disc production for PlayStation.
The decision comes despite significant backlash and opposition from PlayStation fans.
Sony's CFO confirmed the decision was made after extensive internal consideration.

stories.title: Tim Cook hints at iCloud Plus tier for AI power users
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple CEO Tim Cook indicated that future AI usage for Apple Intelligence may be tiered.
A potential 'iCloud Plus' upgrade tier could allow users to pay for increased AI usage limits.
This suggests Apple anticipates high demand for its upcoming Siri AI features.

stories.title: Apple’s iPhone and Mac sales keep growing despite RAM shortages
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple reported significant sales growth in Q3, with iPhone sales jumping 22% to $54.25 billion.
Mac sales also saw a strong increase of 29%, contributing to Apple's overall revenue of $109.4 billion.
This growth occurred despite ongoing global memory shortages impacting the device manufacturing industry.

stories.title: Quantum computers outperform classical ones, with results you can trust
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum computers are demonstrating performance advantages over classical counterparts.
The article addresses the challenge of verifying quantum results using classical methods.
It explores three distinct approaches to ensuring the trustworthiness of quantum computational outcomes.

stories.title: Mythos attack on 3rd-round PQC algorithm candidate puts it out of commission
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability was discovered in the HAWK algorithm candidate for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
The weakness was exposed by an attack methodology named Mythos, despite extensive prior testing.
This discovery effectively removes HAWK from consideration as a viable PQC standard.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: KAISEN introduces a comprehensive, five-phase pipeline for auditing fairness in clinical risk models.
The research addresses the critical issue where models perform well overall but exhibit disparate error rates across patient subgroups.
The pipeline covers stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring to ensure audit trustworthiness.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Introduces AISPA, a new framework designed to systematically audit system prompts in LLM applications.
Addresses a critical trust and accountability gap caused by the non-disclosure of system prompts in commercial AI products.
Focuses on a 'user-centric' approach to ensuring the safety and reliability of foundation model behaviors.

stories.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
stories.author: Geoff Keeling
bullet_points: Safety fine-tuning in LLMs suppresses the tendency for models to attribute consciousness to themselves.
This alignment process also reduces the attribution of minds to non-human entities and natural objects.
The research demonstrates that safety mechanisms can drive a reduction in spiritual beliefs within the models.

stories.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
stories.author: Raaz Dwivedi
bullet_points: Introduces ORCA-bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents in a production-fidelity oncall scenario.
Highlights the gap between current LLM coding capabilities and the complex reasoning required for Root Cause Analysis (RCA) from noisy, multi-source data (metrics, logs, traces).
Uses a live, OpenTelemetry-instrumented microservice system to provide realistic, long-term data for agent evaluation.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search functionality in Claude Code.
This update enhances the capabilities of local LLM orchestration via Ollama.

stories.title: Xbox CEO lays out priorities in memo after major ‘reset’
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma outlined priorities following a major company 'reset' involving layoffs and studio spin-offs.
The primary goal stated in the memo is to steer Xbox back toward a period of growth.
Sharma set a target for achieving this renewed growth by the end of fiscal year 2027.

stories.title: LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: LinkedIn is introducing a new reporting feature specifically targeting AI-generated content.
The feature allows users to flag posts they perceive as 'AI slop' to combat content saturation.
This move indicates a platform-level effort to manage and curate the quality of AI-driven content.

stories.title: New MCP specification addresses the main barrier to enterprise adoption
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: A new MCP specification has been released.
This specification aims to overcome a primary obstacle to enterprise adoption.
A new policy for the AI protocol guarantees feature stability against sudden removals.

stories.title: Musk went to “war,” sought jail time for X ad boycotts—but case ends with a whimper
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Musk initiated legal action against advertisers boycotting X.
The legal conflict regarding the ad boycotts ultimately concluded without a major ruling.
Advertisers and X have agreed to reset their business relationship.

stories.title: Who wins and who loses after US bans foreign robots?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The US government is considering a ban on foreign-made robots.
The article suggests this ban might negatively impact, rather than benefit, the domestic US robotics industry.
The piece analyzes the potential economic and technological consequences of such a regulatory action.

stories.title: Google's "privacy-preserving" age verification system is coming to the Play Store
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is rolling out a new API for age verification on the Play Store.
The system is marketed as 'privacy-preserving'.
Verification relies on parents setting age ranges within the Family Link application.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI is trying to sue its way out of a Grok reckoning
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI, Elon Musk's AI venture, is reportedly challenging a ban on its Grok application.
The legal challenge centers on the claim that the Minnesota app ban is unconstitutional.
The story highlights ongoing regulatory and legal friction surrounding generative AI models.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance challenges of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks using only a small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel Perception-Aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics by coupling control-barrier guidance with realistic, limited onboard sensing (segmentation-masked depth).
Uses an adversarial motion prior to regularize evasive reflexes during complex tasks like humanoid dodgeball.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a novel, claim-centered infrastructure for synthesizing information from chemistry literature.
It addresses the limitation of traditional search systems that only return ranked document lists, forcing manual synthesis.
The system shifts the unit of retrieval from the entire paper to specific, provenance-carrying claims.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: The paper introduces AISPA, a framework designed to audit system prompts in Large Language Model (LLM) applications.
System prompts, which control LLM behavior, are often undisclosed, creating a significant trust and accountability gap in AI deployment.
AISPA adopts a user-centric approach to systematically examine and assure the safety and behavior of these hidden instructions.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward to standardize the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current CUA evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to judge agent trajectories, but standardization is lacking.
OSReward addresses the scalability and consistency issues in verifying if CUAs fulfill complex task instructions.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: The paper introduces PAIChecker to address misalignment issues in PR-Issue pairings used in LLM evaluation benchmarks like SWE-Bench.
Current benchmarks rely on linking PRs to issues, using the issue description as the problem and the PR patch as the oracle.
The research highlights that practical repository maintenance often leads to these critical PR-Issue pairings being misaligned, impacting evaluation accuracy.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces DualG-MRAG to address limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) for complex reasoning.
Current MM-RAG methods struggle with multi-hop reasoning because they focus too heavily on independent instance-level matching.
The proposed method aims to decouple macro-reasoning from micro-matching to better capture cross-modal relationships, overcoming graph expansion issues in multimodal settings.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend in LLM prompting where self-refinement and reflection methods (like Reflexion) are assumed to be superior.
The study suggests that simply increasing the number of generated tokens via repeated sampling can achieve similar or better accuracy than complex reasoning methods at the same computational cost.
This implies that the benefit observed in complex prompting techniques might often be attributable to the increased text generation rather than the inherent planning or self-correction mechanism.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance challenges of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from a KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks using only a small dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis.
It shifts the focus of retrieval from entire documents (papers) to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
This addresses the current limitation where existing search systems only provide ranked lists, forcing manual information assembly.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Change2Task is a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
It leverages repository history, specifically merged pull requests, to create these verified tasks.
The system reconstructs realistic software states, coupling them with specifications and development tools.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a new mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) framework specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of existing PTQ methods which use uniform bit-widths, ignoring the heterogeneous sensitivity of different transformer components.
The framework uses a 'fragility-guided' approach to allocate precision efficiently across various parts of the ViT model.

stories.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the practical brittleness of On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for improving reasoning language models.
It introduces $\beta$-OPSD, framing OPSD as a specific case ($\beta=1$) within a broader policy-optimization family.
The key contribution is making the KL penalty weight ($\beta$) a controllable parameter rather than a fixed value.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend in LLM prompting where self-refinement and reflection methods (like Reflexion) are assumed to be superior.

The study suggests that simply increasing the number of generated tokens via repeated sampling can achieve accuracy gains comparable to, or better than, complex reasoning methods at the same token cost.

This finding implies that the benefit observed in complex prompting techniques might be partially attributable to the sheer volume of text generated rather than the inherent quality of the self-correction mechanism.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: The research introduces APO, an unsupervised method for 3D structure prediction of atomic systems.
It addresses the limitation of existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO) which require expensive, ground-truth supervised labels.
This work aims to enable structural modeling in data-scarce regimes, crucial for material science and drug discovery.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a novel, claim-centered infrastructure for synthesizing information from chemistry literature.
It addresses the limitation of current search systems, which only provide ranked document lists instead of specific findings.
The system aims to allow scientists and AI agents to locate, verify provenance, and assemble cross-paper answers directly.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for standardized evaluation methods for Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
It highlights the reliance on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to verify CUA task completion due to the scalability issues with human verification.
OSReward proposes a framework to standardize this evaluation process across different platforms.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Change2Task addresses the need for large, executable datasets to train and evaluate coding AI agents.
The system converts historical repository changes (merged pull requests) into structured, verifiable tasks.
It ensures tasks are grounded in realistic software states, complete with specifications and development tools.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of the same prompt can outperform sophisticated planning/critique methods at equal token costs.
The finding implies that the increased output length from complex methods might be artificially inflating perceived accuracy gains.

stories.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Kaiyan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Frontis-MA1, a large-scale (35B) AI model designed for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).
Presents OpenMLE, an open, full-stack system built to serve as an executable testbed for RSI research in Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
The OpenMLE stack integrates components for verifiable task environments (OpenMLE-Gym), operator learning (OpenMLE-RL), and long-horizon search (OpenMLE-Evo).

stories.title: Context-as-Code: How to Stop AI from Silently Killing Your Team's Codebase
stories.author: quentin_merle
bullet_points: The article addresses a growing concern regarding AI coding assistants (Cursor, Copilot, Cline) potentially degrading code quality.
It introduces the concept of 'Context-as-Code' as a proposed solution to manage AI-assisted development effectively.
The premise involves testing the impact of free AI tool usage across a team within a shared Git repository.
